articles.title: 12 Years Ago, 'Doctor Who's Most Unhinged Episode Revealed the Doctor at His Worst
articles.summary: Doctor Who has never shied away from showing the Doctor at his worst. In “A Good Man Goes to War,” Eleven (Matt Smith) realizes that his choices have made him nearly as monstrous as his enemies.
body: But one episode rarely gets the recognition it deserves for portraying the Doctor at his most unhinged and hypocritical.

“The Caretaker,” which aired in 2014, is hardly a memorable monster-of-the-week episode. Twelve (Peter Capaldi) goes undercover as a janitor at companion Clara Oswald’s ( Jenna Coleman ) school, Coal Hill, to deal with an alien robot called the Skovox Blitzer.

The robot can destroy Earth, and it looks cool, but it’s the episode’s least interesting element. Instead, writer Gareth Roberts turns “The Caretaker” into a character drama about the meeting between Twelve and Clara’s boyfriend, Danny Pink (Samuel Anderson).

Throughout most of the season, Clara has been juggling two very different lives: her “normie” life as an English teacher, where she’s dating fellow teacher Danny, and her life-changing adventures with the Doctor across time and space. In “The Caretaker,” those worlds finally collide, making for an uncomfortable encounter all around.
points: Doctor Who has never shied away from showing the Doctor at his worst.
In “A Good Man Goes to War,” Eleven (Matt Smith) realizes that his choices have made him nearly as monstrous as his enemies.
But one episode rarely gets the recognition it deserves for portraying the Doctor at his most unhinged and hypocritical.
“The Caretaker,” which aired in 2014, is hardly a memorable monster-of-the-week episode.

articles.title: 50 Years Later, the Best War Series of All Time Is Still Unlike Anything Else on TV
articles.summary: When Robert Altman's M*A*S*H arrived in theaters in 1970, its irreverent approach to the Korean War was unlike anything audiences had seen before. The film followed army surgeons who used practical jokes, alcohol, and a disregard for military authority to maintain their sanity while treating the…
body: Over 11 seasons, M*A*S*H evolved from a sitcom about wisecracking doctors into a thoughtful examination of humanity. The doctors and nurses of the 4077th Mobile Army Surgical Hospital are exhausted, frightened, and overwhelmed by circumstances beyond their control. They're also funny, largely because humor is one of the few weapons they have against the horrors surrounding them.

I grew up watching M*A*S*H with my parents, and while the jokes made me laugh, what stayed with me was how much I cared about the people telling them. Hawkeye Pierce (Alan Alda), Margaret "Hot Lips" Houlihan (Loretta Swit), Radar O'Reilly (Gary Burghoff) and the rest of the ensemble feel more like people you know, making their triumphs more satisfying and their heartbreaks more devastating.
More than half a century after its premiere, M*A*S*H, available to stream on Hulu, remains remarkable because it understood how closely laughter and heartbreak are connected.
points: When Robert Altman's M*A*S*H arrived in theaters in 1970, its irreverent approach to the Korean War was unlike anything audiences had seen before.
Over 11 seasons, M*A*S*H evolved from a sitcom about wisecracking doctors into a thoughtful examination of humanity.

articles.summary: Hello, it is me, your regular weekend host Mertie and I am here once again to guide you gently into Saturday with our usual feature What We've Been Playing, where we write a little about the games we've been, yes, playing.
body: But enough about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Do tell all! And don't forget we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your leisurely perusal, just in case you forgot what you were playing a year or a month or a week ago.

I'm a little busy outside of work at the moment with rehearsals for a play I'm in (The Importance of Being Ernest), but I did find time for another Dungeons & Dragons first: a one-on-one game. I've been wanting to do one of these for a while, and, as I discovered recently, one-on-one games are a whole thing. Duets, they're called, rather poetically. You need to modify campaigns a bit to be playable this way, because most are designed for groups of four or five people, and you probably need to give a player a companion character as backup. But otherwise, it's totally doable. Some people make adventures exclusively for one-on-one games.

articles.title: Aaron Paul Makes Surprise Cameo in DC’s Clayface
articles.summary: Spoilers follow for Clayface, which is now playing in theaters. Three-time Emmy winner Aaron Paul has a blink and you’ll miss it cameo in the new DC movie Clayface. Now, the film’s director, James Watkins, has revealed why the Breaking Bad and Westworld star is in DC’s first R-rated horror movie.
body: Paul plays Jimmy “One Nut” Hagen, the late abusive father of protagonist Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries). Word of Paul’s casting was first reported by Feature First back in June.

Paul’s cameo occurs during the climactic action sequence set at the Gotham City nightclub Vesuvius where Matt confronts the gangsters who disfigured him. Matt finds the hood who killed his dad and morphs into his father to shock the killer.

Paul originally had a larger supporting role in Clayface, appearing in flashbacks to Matt’s youth, but the filmmakers ultimately cut nearly all of those scenes. Paul’s appearance in the nightclub is all that remains of his role.
“In terms of trying to figure out the character, it was, How much is Matt defined by his past and how much is he an everyman?” Watkins told Entertainment Weekly.

articles.title: J.J. Abrams’ Best Original Sci-Fi Movie Officially Finds a New Home on Streaming
articles.summary: In early 2006, J.J. Abrams was in the midst of a generational run. Alias was about to end, Lost had become a cultural phenomenon, and Abrams was traveling the world promoting his directorial debut with Mission: Impossible 3. Somehow, Abrams was just getting started.
body: At Paramount’s 2007 San Diego Comic-Con panel, Abrams said that while promoting MI3 in Japan, he had visited a toy store with his son. He wanted Godzilla toys. Abrams wanted “our own monster,” something “insane and intense,” rather than King Kong, who he called “adorable.” So he decided to make a movie about one.

That’s how Cloverfield was born. Abrams tapped Lost writer Drew Goddard to write the script and longtime collaborator Matt Reeves to direct. The first teaser appeared before Transformers in July 2007. At Comic-Con, Abrams showed a poster of a beheaded Statue of Liberty looming over a smoky New York City. No title. No actors. Just a release date: Jan. 18, 2008. Keep in mind, this was the same panel that showed early footage from Iron Man, Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull, and Abrams’ live-action Star Trek.

Say what you will about some of his less-loved work, but Abrams knows how to generate hype and mystery. Cloverfield, newly streaming on Peacock (but also available on Paramount Plus and for free on Pluto TV), is worthy of both.

articles.title: Dead by Daylight to Remove Chucky Content Just Months After Losing Michael Myers
articles.summary: Dead by Daylight fans are beside themselves after Behaviour Interactive announced that all Chucky content would no longer be available to purchase starting next month.
body: The developer behind the popular asymmetrical horror game confirmed plans to pull the Chucky Chapter from sale in posts shared across social media. The message followed rumors that the possessed killer doll would soon be removed from the game, with the official statement promising that those who have purchased related content will be able to use it even after it is removed from shelves starting November 24, 2026.

"We welcomed The Good Guy out of his box and into The Fog nearly three years ago, but it's now time for the Chucky Chapter to leave the shelf," Behaviour said. "On November 24, 2026, the Chapter and its associated content will be removed from in-game and first-party stores. Any content unlocked before that date will remain available to use in-game."

As detailed in an FAQ post shared by the developers, these changes to the Chucky Chapter mean a few things for Dead by Daylight players. Its Killer, known in-game as The Good Guy, will no longer be available to purchase, though bug fixes will still be supported. The collection of outfits and cosmetics he's gained since being added in 2023 will also be made unavailable, and no future add-ons for the character will be added.

body: Marvel Studios and directors Joe and Anthony Russo almost certainly have plans for plenty of superhero moments and surprises. How Hüller fits into that plan remains to be seen, but considering fans had already speculated about her involvement in recent days, some of the less patient Marvel Cinematic Universe enjoyers are probably already doing their best to piece together Doomsday's mysteries early.

Hüller is a German actor with a decades-long career on movie and TV screens. She was nominated for Actress in a Leading Role at the 2024 Oscars for her part in Anatomy of a Fall, but is also known for her parts in films like Digger, The Zone of Interest, and Fatherland. articles.title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s First DLC Is Out Now, Honors A Real Soldier Who Sustained Gruesome Injuries
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 released today, October 23, and the game's first DLC pack is available now. In keeping with Call of Duty tradition, the day-one DLC is a Call of Duty Endowment (CODE) pack, with proceeds going to Activision's charity that supports military veterans find new jobs after…
body: The CODE Valor Pack adds the real-life Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter to the game as a playable character.

Carpenter was in Marjah, Afghanistan, when, on November 21, 2010, he put himself in front of a grenade to help save the life of his fellow Marine, Nick Eufrazio. Carpenter sustained serious injuries from the grenade blast. He was unconscious for five weeks, had his teeth stripped from his mouth, and lost an eye. He sustained numerous other life-threatening injuries in the blast.

Carpenter underwent brain surgery to remove shrapnel from his head. He had about 40 other surgeries to addresses his injuries, which included a collapsed lung, fractured fingers, and one arm that broke in more than 30 places. He had multiple skin grafts and now has a prosthetic eye, a new jaw, and new teeth.

The Valor Pack includes the Relentless and Valor skins, along with new weapon blueprints, a combat knife, and a weapon charm, among other things. All proceeds from the $20 DLC bundles will go to the CODE charity.
points: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 released today, October 23, and the game's first DLC pack is available now.

articles.title: The Witcher's Geralt Officially Returns for New Adventure
articles.summary: The Witcher fans have had a lot to look forward to, like a remaster of The Witcher 3, the Songs of the Past expansion, and The Witcher 4, expected sometime in 2028. Those fans probably know by now that their favorite monster-hunting games are based on an iconic book series (as is the Netflix show…
body: At a recent convention appearance in Poland, Sapkowski confirmed he's working on the next Witcher book and that he should be finished writing it by the end of 2027. According to Witcher news site Redanian Intelligence, expect it to once again star Geralt; Sapkowski said he doesn't intend to write any Witcher books about other characters, like Yennefer.

The latest The Witcher book was 2025's The Witcher: Crossroads of Ravens. It was a prequel about young Geralt's first big adventure as a Witcher. As Geralt is middle-aged during the short story collections and novels, there are plenty of years of his life left unexplored, and Sapkowski knows it.

In an interview with IGN, he said, "Sky is the limit," when asked if there's room to delve further into Geralt's formative years in more prequels. He also said, "I am considering writing more short stories." The Witcher series began with a short story, and Sapkowski published two collections before the first novel, Blood of Elves.
Still, he finds writing short stories to be a unique challenge. "It is not an easy thing to create a good short story. This is much more difficult than writing a novel," Sapkowski said.
points: The Witcher fans have had a lot to look forward to, like a remaster of The Witcher 3, the Songs of the Past expansion, and The Witcher 4, expected sometime in 2028.

body: She added: "I’m holding hope for magic to happen. This community and you incredible vevs deserve that and more."

A "Save Mass Effect" Change.org petition was launched this week to urge EA to "take decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect." The petition has more than 65,000 signatures so far.

All of BioWare's new releases in the past decade--Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard--were commercial disappointments. Against that backdrop, closing the studio makes a lot of financial sense, but it's upsetting to the millions of Mass Effect fans who adore the franchise and want to see it continue.
Based on insider reporting, the new Mass Effect game would have mixed covert ops with John Wick-inspired action, and that got a lot of people excited about what could have been.

body: Known for his lore videos, including several on Mass Effect, Dantics says he was part of a private "Mass Effect Council," a community feedback group of content creators who helped advise BioWare's small team.

Dantics says that Mass Effect Universe was set over 600 years after the Reaper War, and players would step into the boots of a customizable N7 agent. Players would also have a much smaller arsenal of weapons that would make them feel like a "cross between John Wick and James Bond," and they'd be working to take down a sinister force that was operating in the shadows of a galactic cold war. While Commander Shepard was a soldier, your N7 character was going to be an "agent" who would rely on cunning to get through encounters, but could apply pressure when needed--ballistic pressure, that is.

articles.title: Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto says even if gen-AI "were to eventually handle everything, there will always be a role left" for human designers
articles.summary: Legendary Nintendo developer Shigeru Miyamoto - who led development on classic games such as Super Mario 64 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time - has argued that the rise of generative AI tools won't necessarily replace human talent.
body: Next month, Shigeru Miyamoto will become the first ever video game developer to be awarded the Order of Culture by the Emperor of Japan, a hugely prestigious honour. But in a recent press conference dedicated to the award, he also shared some thoughts about gen-AI and its use in game production.

"Our generation lived through a period of rapid computer development - a time when tools were constantly evolving, moving from typewriters to word processors,” he said while speaking to the press, in quotes translated by VGC. Miyamoto argued that a designer's true capabilities "finally came to the fore" as technology advanced and was capable of handling more of what might be considered "labor", and a similar transition may take place with generative AI tech.

"While the act of creation is inherently satisfying, there's a danger: one might find satisfaction in the labor itself and mistakenly believe that a high-quality piece of work has been created," he added. If generative-AI software replaces more tasks involved in game production, human game devs might have "an opportunity to reflect on what's really important."

articles.title: WoW: Forever’s Divisive Layering Will See Major Improvements For Launch, Blizzard Says
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's layering system will receive some significant improvements for launch, according to a statement provided to GameSpot from Blizzard. Layering, for the uninitiated, is a behind-the-scenes system in WoW: Forever that essentially creates and runs new versions (or layers) of…
body: There are some pros to this system. It makes completing quests easier (since there's less competition for quests items and enemies) and the world far less crowded. It also helps performance, as anytime there are thousands of players in a concentrated area, like a capital city, the game can struggle to handle the load. Layering spreads those players out. It works wonders in modern WoW and has also been used to different degrees in various versions of WoW Classic in the past.

Unfortunately, there are also some huge downsides that have repeatedly surfaced over the course of the WoW: Forever beta. It doesn't take much searching on YouTube or Reddit to find countless instances of players complaining about layering. Leaving a group, crossing into a different zone, or traveling on a zeppelin or boat causes players to abruptly switch layers. The layering changes feel far more frequent and noticeable than in the past, ruining some of the charm that comes from having a persistent world filled with the same people.
points: World of Warcraft: Forever's layering system will receive some significant improvements for launch, according to a statement provided to GameSpot from Blizzard.

videos.title: Monster Hunter Wilds – Demo Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: Start your Monster Hunter Wilds adventure early on Nintendo Switch 2 with the free Prologue Demo!
body: Head into the Forbidden Lands, then carry your save data over to the full game! The demo supports local play too, so gather your fellow hunters.

Journey to the Forbidden Lands and take on the thrilling monsters that await, then prepare yourself for Master Rank and the launch of the massive expansion, Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, coming to Nintendo Switch 2 at launch in 2027.
